passage:
You want to stay out till ten for the concert? Sit down, I'm Joseph, and I'll tell you about my mother's curfew.

When I was twenty and living at home in Kochi, my mother Reena wanted me indoors by eight. My friends laughed. I was angry enough to plan to climb the back wall, and I stood on the compound wall once before I got down.

Instead I asked her why. She said quietly, "A neighbour's son had a bad accident on that road at night." I hadn't known.

I said, "I'll message you when I reach each place and when I leave, and I'll be on time for a month. Then can we try nine?" It took two months, not one, but she moved it to nine-thirty. Some nights I sent "reached" even when it felt silly. That's how nine-thirty happened.

qa.q: What time did Reena first want Joseph home?
What was Reena worried about when she set the curfew?
qa.a: Fear for Joseph's safety. A neighbour's son had a bad accident on that road at night.

qa.q: What did Joseph offer instead of sneaking out?
qa.a: He offered to message when he reached each place and when he left, and to be on time for a month before asking for a later hour.

qa.q: How might Joseph's friends have seen his eight o'clock curfew?
qa.a: They laughed, so they probably saw it as strict or embarrassing, without knowing about the neighbour's son's accident on that road.

grounding: Joseph's mother sets a curfew out of worry; he asks about the fear, offers check-ins and earns more freedom by reliability instead of sneaking around.

passage:
Dear Mummy,
You won't believe it, but I'm writing you a letter. Well, an email. Rekha didi says you'll listen properly if I put it in writing, so please hear me out before you say no.
I know the 9 p.m. rule comes from worry, especially since Sameer bhaiya's accident last year. I was there too; I remember how you didn't sleep for days. I'm not trying to make you feel that again.
But my robotics team works till 10 on build nights, and I've been leaving early and feeling like a kid. Twice I almost said the lab closed late. I didn't want to start lying to you.
Here's what I'm asking: on Tuesdays and Thursdays, can I stay till 10? I'll share my live location, message when I leave, and take the auto with Kunal, who lives two lanes away. If I miss a single check-in, we go back to 9, no argument.
Can we try it for a month?
Nilesh

qa.q: What time is the current rule?
Why did Nilesh not use the "lab closed late" excuse?
qa.a: Nilesh felt tempted but uneasy, not wanting to start lying to a worried mother.
Live location, a message on leaving, sharing the auto with Kunal, and going back to 9 if Nilesh misses a single check-in.

qa.q: What is behind Mummy's 9 p.m. rule?
qa.a: Fear after Sameer bhaiya's accident, when she didn't sleep for days.

grounding: Shows a curfew set out of a parent's worry, and answering with talk about the fear, offered check-ins and earning freedom through reliability.

passage:
Ojas, you remember first year, when I used to climb over the back wall after the 9 o'clock hostel gate? Yeah. That was me being an idiot.
My parents had signed the strictest option on the hostel form. I thought they didn't trust me at all. So I sneaked out for a friend's birthday, twisted my ankle coming down the wall, and had to call the warden from the road at midnight. Imagine that phone call to my father.
He wasn't just angry. He sounded scared. That's what got me.
So in second year I asked them to sit with me on a video call. I said, "What exactly are you afraid of?" Mummy said, "Late buses, bad roads, and you not answering." Fair.
We agreed: I'd text whenever I left anywhere after 9, and answer every call. Three months, no missed calls. Then they changed the form to 11.
So yeah, I'm Tejas, the guy who learned that being reliable works better than climbing walls.

qa.q: What time did the hostel gate close?
What made Tejas feel different during the midnight call with his father?
qa.a: Hearing his father sound scared, not just angry, made Tejas feel guilty and see the fear behind the rule.

qa.q: How did Tejas earn later timings?
qa.a: He asked his parents what they feared, agreed to text after 9 and answer every call, and kept it up for three months.
Late buses, bad roads, and Tejas not answering.

grounding: Illustrates sneaking around a curfew, then talking about the parents' fear, offering check-ins and earning freedom by reliability.
